# ARCH-14: Do not add code before it is used, and remove what your change leaves unused

- Code that nothing calls costs flash on every board and review time, and rots, since nothing exercises it. A PR adds methods, members, parameters and options only when something in it uses them (rmackay9, [#11795](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/11795): "a golden rule in AP that we don't add things before they are used"); a helper first used by a later PR belongs in that PR, or that PR stacks on this one.
- When a change replaces a mechanism or stops calling a helper, the old one goes in the same PR (peterbarker, [#31919](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/31919): "why are we keeping any of the old calibration code?"). That is what "required by the change" means in the Surgical Modification Principle; dead code the change did not touch is a separate PR. Removing something users see - a parameter, a log field, a mode - is still governed by [ARCH-6](ARCH-6.md).

Confirmed 2026-10-16. Part of the root playbook, under [Architectural Principles](../claude/CLAUDE.md#architectural-principles). [All architectural rules](../README.md#architectural-rules)
